script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Workplace
Theme: ambition

Begin screenplay.

FADE IN:

INT. GLASS OFFICE - DAY

The office, a modern open-plan space, hums with the sound of keyboards clacking and phones ringing. A sea of computers and desks, whitewashed walls and glass partitions.

NICOLAS, a young and ambitious intern, sits at a desk, head down, typing furiously on his laptop. He is surrounded by more seasoned colleagues, all heads buried in their work.

Suddenly, his supervisor, SARAH, enters. Sarah is a formidable woman in her late 40s, with sharp features and a steely gaze.

SARAH
(looking over Nicola's shoulder)
What have we here? A report on the latest marketing trends? Impressive.

NICOLAS
(looking up, flustered)
Yes, I've been researching the latest trends and implementing them into our campaigns. I thought it might help us attract new clients.

SARAH
(impressed)
You're a quick learner. I like that. But we need more than just trends to attract new business. We need ideas.

NICOLAS
(nervously)
Ideas? I'm not sure I follow.

Sarah hands him a folder.

SARAH
Take a look at these past campaigns. They were successful because they were innovative, not just because they followed the latest trends. Think outside the box. Come up with something fresh and original.

NICOLAS
(taking the folder)
I will, I promise.

INT. COFFEE SHOP - LATER

Nicola sits in a corner booth, laptop open, surrounded by the sounds of clinking cups and chatter. He stares blankly at the screen, fingers hovering above the keys.

Suddenly, he hears a voice.

ELLEN, a fellow intern, sits down across from him. She's quiet, unassuming, but there's a quiet intelligence in her eyes.

ELLEN
(smiling)
Stuck?

NICOLAS
(startled)
Yes, I can't seem to come up with any good ideas.

ELLEN
(leaning forward)
Have you tried brainstorming with the team? Bouncing ideas off each other?

NICOLAS
(shaking his head)
No, I wanted to come up with something on my own first.

ELLEN
(smiling)
Well, if you change your approach, you might find that collaboration is the key to success.

INT. OFFICE - NIGHT

Nicola and Ellen sit in the empty office, surrounded by the quiet hum of the air conditioning. They bounce ideas off each other, laughing and joking as they build on each other's thoughts.

They come up with a campaign idea that is innovative, fresh, and original. They're excited and proud of their work.

INT. BOARDROOM - DAY

The team presents their campaign idea to Sarah and the rest of the executives. They are met with enthusiasm and praise.

SARAH
(smiling)
This is exactly what we needed. Nicola and Ellen, I'm proud of you both.

NICOLAS and ELLEN exchange proud glances. They've worked together to achieve something great.

FADE OUT.

THE END
